archetype.name: Treadmill Team (run-first)
archetype.definition: A club that keeps landing between four and eight wins, built around a good Bijan Robinson run game and an average defense, held back by a passing attack and ball security that are among the league's worst.

report.headline: A real run game stapled to a passing attack that keeps giving it away
report.take:
Atlanta at 3-7 is a familiar team. The history block shows seven or eight wins in six of the last eight seasons, almost always with a negative point differential and a poor cover rate. This year's version fits the pattern with one twist. The identity is now the ground game. Bijan Robinson has 185 carries, the rushing offense ranks 8th in EPA per play, and the offense passes less than expected more than almost anyone (-6.7, 28th). With Michael Penix Jr. starting every week since Week 3, the passing game ranks 29th in EPA per play.

The record is not a luck story. The point differential of -57 implies about 3.9 wins, and wins over expected sit at only -0.86, so this is roughly what the team has earned. What drives the losses is turnovers: 19 giveaways against 10 takeaways. The 5-giveaway home loss to Carolina, the 4-turnover shutout in Tampa and three more against Chicago are the defining games. When Penix protects the ball the team looks competent: 35 points at Green Bay, 45 at New Orleans, a clean win over San Francisco. When he doesn't, the run game never gets to matter. Special teams leak hidden yards every week (29th), and the team hasn't won a one-score game.

The numbers hide some things about the line. It allows the 2nd-lowest pressure rate and the fewest QB hits in the league, but the ball also comes out faster than almost anywhere (time to throw 2.624, 30th of 31). The low pressure is partly the quick, short game protecting itself, which also helps explain why the passing produces so little. The run game is similar: elite stuff rate and yards per carry, but only 25th in yards before contact. That is Robinson making yards after contact, not the line clearing space. The defense is truly middle of the pack, 14th in EPA allowed and 6th in QB hit rate, but it gives up explosive runs (30th) and loses on third down (24th).

The trend is bad. The last three games were double-digit losses, including a Kansas City game where 286 passing yards came with -14.6 passing EPA. The schedule still has three division games in a NFC South whose leader is 4-5, so the math isn't dead. The team playing now, though, looks like a five- or six-win club unless the giveaways dry up.

strengths.title: Bijan's run game carries the offense
strengths.body: The rushing attack is a top-tier unit: 4.68 yards per carry, one of the lowest stuff rates in the league, and rushing EPA ranked 8th. Robinson is creating most of it himself, because the line ranks 25th in yards before contact. That makes it sustainable as long as he stays healthy, but it is a back-driven strength, not a scheme that works without him.

strengths.title: Quarterback stays clean
strengths.body: Atlanta allows the 2nd-lowest pressure rate and the fewest QB hits in football. Part of that is design: few teams get the ball out faster. The protection itself is real, but the clean pockets come from a quick game that doesn't threaten defenses downfield, so it hasn't turned into passing efficiency.

strengths.title: Pass rush that gets home
strengths.body: The defense hits quarterbacks at the 6th-highest rate and pressures at the 10th-highest. Those hits aren't becoming sacks (sack rate 21st), but a rush this disruptive keeps the defense around league average even when the coverage behind it isn't special. It is the most stable part of the defense.

concerns.title: Giveaways are deciding games
concerns.body: Nineteen turnovers and a -9 differential explain more of the record than anything else. The giveaways came in clusters that turned games into blowouts: five against Carolina, four in Tampa. Some regression toward fewer giveaways is normal, but with the starter in his eighth start and the passing game this inefficient, this is more than bad luck.

concerns.title: Passing game doesn't move the ball
concerns.body: Passing EPA per play ranks 29th, and the staff is hiding it by running far more than situations call for. The KC loss showed the problem: plenty of yards, deeply negative value, because the yards came underneath and late. Until the pass game makes defenses pay downfield, the offense depends on Robinson and stalls whenever it falls behind.

concerns.title: Chunk runs and third downs
concerns.body: The defense allows explosive runs at the 3rd-highest rate and ranks 24th on third down, so drives it nearly stops keep going anyway. Tampa ran for 324 yards and Baltimore for 208, which shows a front that can be beaten by committed run teams. This is a structural flaw, not a small-sample fluke.

trend.note: The Weeks 3-4 surge under Penix (35 and 45 points) and the SF upset now look like the peak. The last three games were a shutout in Tampa followed by double-digit home losses to Cincinnati and Kansas City.

nextGame.headline: Bijan versus the league's best defense, with ball security deciding it
nextGame.body:
Atlanta comes off a bye to face a 7-2 Minnesota team that wins in a way Atlanta can't match. The Vikings' defense is 1st in EPA allowed, 1st against the pass, 1st in pressure rate and 1st in sack rate, and they lead the league in special teams EPA. Their offense is among the worst in football (30th in EPA per play), and wins over expected of 2.12 say the record outruns the play. The real opening is the Vikings' run defense profile. Offenses run against them more than against anyone (the strongest run funnel in the league), and they allow explosive runs at a high rate with a below-average missed-tackle rate. That is where Robinson can attack. Through the air, Atlanta's quick game is the right answer to the league's best pass rush, but it is also exactly the kind of passing that hasn't produced value.

Availability favors Atlanta on the Vikings' side. Kyler Murray is out with a hamstring strain, with a return estimate that falls on game day, and Kirk Cousins started the last game. Jordan Addison needs thumb surgery and will miss weeks. Jauan Jennings, T.J. Hockenson, Blake Cashman and edge Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins were all out as of the latest report, though most carry earlier return estimates, and Andrew Van Ginkel is questionable. A thin receiving room behind a backup quarterback is a real break for an average Atlanta pass defense. Atlanta is missing linebacker Divine Deablo, a 78% snap player, which hurts a run defense already prone to chunk plays, plus reserve receiver Zachariah Branch.

waysToWin.title: Ride Bijan into the run funnel
waysToWin.body: Minnesota's elite pass defense pushes offenses to run, and it gives up explosive runs more often than most. Atlanta's best unit is its ground game, and the run-heavy approach is already its default. Staying on schedule with Robinson keeps Penix out of obvious passing downs against the league's top pressure.

waysToWin.title: Hit a short-handed Vikings offense
waysToWin.body: Minnesota's offense ranks near the bottom in EPA and allows one of the highest sack rates, and it may be without its starting quarterback and several receivers. Atlanta's rush ranks 6th in QB hit rate. Turning those hits into sacks would keep the Vikings from scoring on their own, so this becomes a low-scoring game that a couple of Robinson runs can decide.

waysToWin.title: Quick throws to Drake London
waysToWin.body: Minnesota has been efficient against most receiving roles but gives up value to opposing WR1s (27th in EPA per target). London has 79 targets, by far the team's most. Quick, defined throws to him beat the pressure before it arrives and are the least risky way to complete passes in this game.

waysToLose.title: Gifting a takeaway defense
waysToLose.body: Minnesota is 2nd in turnover differential and Atlanta is 26th. Against a defense this good, Atlanta can't recover from short fields or lost possessions. Two Penix giveaways are probably enough to decide it, because Minnesota rarely needs to drive the length of the field to win.

waysToLose.title: Falling behind into passing downs
waysToLose.body: If Atlanta trails early, it has to throw into the league's best pass defense and its top pressure rate with a passing game that ranks 29th. That is how the Tampa and Kansas City games went wrong. Game script would remove the one thing Atlanta does well.

waysToLose.title: Losing the hidden-yardage game
waysToLose.body: The special teams gap is the largest in the league: Atlanta is 29th and Minnesota 1st. In a low-scoring game, that alone can flip field position and points. Atlanta also hasn't won a one-score game, while Minnesota keeps winning them.

nextGame.watch: Atlanta's early-down run success: if Robinson keeps Penix in second- or third-and-short, Atlanta can stay in a low-scoring game, and if not, Minnesota's pass rush takes over.

restOfSeason.body:
After Minnesota come Detroit and two road trips to Cleveland and Washington, then three straight division games against Tampa, New Orleans and Carolina. The division is weak enough that those last three matter: the leader is 4-5. The sustainable parts are Robinson's run game, the clean pockets and a pass rush that keeps the defense near average. The turnover rate is the most likely thing to improve simply by regressing toward normal. Still, Atlanta's history of negative turnover margins and Penix's struggles mean improvement shouldn't be assumed. Since wins over expected are only slightly negative, there's no hidden luck dividend coming either.

Realistically this looks like another five-to-seven-win finish, in line with the last eight seasons. A division title only becomes possible if the passing game moves from bottom-five toward average. The run defense's habit of allowing explosive plays is a problem against Detroit and Tampa, and the special teams drag will keep costing close games.
swingFactors: Results in the three closing division games

confidence.note: Ten games with a stable starter since Week 3 and a long track record; turnover swings make game-to-game results noisy.
